title: echo-agent-extension-v1
description: echo-agent SDK extension contract over stable ACP v1. Standard ACP types are owned by the official agent-client-protocol-schema artifact and are intentionally absent from this document.

WireDuration.title: WireDuration
WireDuration.description: Rust `Duration` represented without collapsing the full `u64` seconds range into an overflowing nanosecond count.

WireTimestamp.title: WireTimestamp
WireTimestamp.description: Signed Unix seconds plus a positive sub-second component. This represents instants before and after the epoch without relying on JSON safe integers.

HandleKind.title: HandleKind
HandleKind.description: What kind of framework object a handle refers to. Typed kinds keep stale errors diagnosable across the wire.

generation.description: Monotonic generation of the owning Host; incremented across restarts so pre-restart handles fail as stale instead of rebinding.

id.description: Non-empty domain identity assigned by the framework.

WireHandle.title: WireHandle
WireHandle.description:
Opaque handle to a framework object: non-empty domain id + generation.

Ids are strings assigned by the framework authority; the SDK never interprets their content, never exposes memory addresses, and never reuses an id across kinds.

WireValue.title: WireValue
WireValue.description: Closed structural value algebra used by manifest-identified facade operations. It avoids an unbounded, schema-free `serde_json::Value` escape hatch while still preserving records, variants and unknown values.

fields.description: Bounded key/value facts; values are strings, never raw payloads.

oneOf.description: Peer does not speak a compatible ACP wire protocol version.
Peer's `_echo_agent` extension protocol version is incompatible.
Extension contract/source digest mismatch.
Required extension capability missing or unsupported.
Malformed request (structure, method usage, ordering).
Semantically invalid configuration.
Semantically invalid value (scalars, paths, payload shapes).
Operation requires a feature the Host was not compiled with.
Handle generation no longer matches the live object.
Handle refers to an object that has been closed/destroyed.
Framework returned a typed domain error.
Registered extension rejected the invocation.
Registered extension failed while executing.
Extension invocation exceeded its deadline.
Extension's SDK connection is gone.
Invocation conflicts with an exclusive in-flight callback of the same registration (re-entrant mutation). Re-entry returns this typed conflict instead of waiting for the holder (design §12.3).
Operation was cancelled; framework terminal state remains authoritative.
Host is shutting down and refuses new work.
Host process exited before the operation settled.
Consumer fell below the retained watermark.
Replay is unavailable for the requested window.
Payload exceeds the negotiated bound.
Payload violates the extension serialization contract.

ExtensionErrorCode.title: ExtensionErrorCode
ExtensionErrorCode.description: Stable extension error codes. Codes are closed: reusing a retired code for a different meaning is a breaking protocol change (design §18).

Retryability.title: Retryability
Retryability.description: Whether an operation may be retried and when (design §10.6). Only the framework's own operation contract decides to actually retry; this field tells language SDKs what is *safe* to retry.

handle.description: Handle the error refers to, when applicable.

operation.description: Domain operation identity (e.g. `run/start`), independent from any JSON-RPC request id.

stream.description: Live event stream the envelope belongs to; the generation fence prevents a pre-restart subscriber from consuming a newer stream.

after_sequence.description: Replay events strictly after this sequence (0 = from the retained beginning).

stream.description: Event stream to replay. The handle's generation must match the currently served stream incarnation; stale or wrong-kind handles fail with typed errors before any event is read.

requested_after_sequence.description: Cursor supplied by the request. This makes an empty response and a retention gap independently verifiable.

stream.description: Event stream that hit its live-delivery bound.

CapabilityDeclaration.description: One declared capability. Required capabilities must be understood by the SDK client for initialization to succeed; optional ones may be ignored.

EchoLimits.description: Resource bounds the Host enforces (design §10.2/§16). All bounds are inclusive maxima; exceeding them fails with the matching typed extension error instead of unbounded growth.

max_extension_descriptor_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes of one extension registration descriptor.

max_extension_payload_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes of one extension invocation input or result.

max_extension_stream_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes of one extension stream chunk payload.

max_inflight_extension_invocations.description: Maximum simultaneously in-flight reverse invocations per connection.

max_message_bytes.description: Maximum serialized request/response payload in bytes.

max_open_handles.description: Maximum simultaneously issued (open) Agent/Session/Run/Stream handles per connection.

max_outstanding_live_events.description: Maximum not-yet-acknowledged live events per stream. Reaching this bound emits one gap notification and pauses live delivery until the Client acknowledges a cursor (`_echo_agent/event/ack`).

max_registered_extensions.description: Maximum simultaneously registered extension implementations per connection. Registration is connection-owned and never persists across a Host restart or a reconnect.

max_replay_bytes.description: Maximum cumulative serialized event bytes returned by one replay.

max_replay_events.description: Maximum events returned by one replay request.

max_stream_buffer_bytes.description: Maximum cumulative serialized live event bytes per stream before the gap/pause behavior above applies.

max_stream_buffer_events.description: Maximum events buffered per subscriber before backpressure/gap.

max_structured_output_bytes.description: Maximum structured output payload in bytes.

ExtensionCapability.description: Extension capabilities the Host may expose. Each maps to a family of `_echo_agent/*` methods; the method catalog asserts that every method's required capability is declared here.

oneOf.description: `agent/*` construction, description and close.
`session/*` extension handles beyond standard ACP sessions.
`run/*` start, wait, steer, cancel and receipts.
`run/replay` bounded event replay and gap reporting.
`task/*` TaskRun/PlanTask graph operations.
`subagent/*` dispatch and control.
`extension/*` registration and reverse invocation bridge.
Structured output contracts on runs.

capabilities.description: Declared extension capabilities with required/optional flag.

contract_digest.description: Digest of the extension contract (schema + catalog), computed by the schema export tool and pinned in the contract artifacts.

extension_protocol_version.description: `_echo_agent` extension protocol version (governed independently from the ACP wire version and crate versions, design §18).

features.description: Leaf Cargo features compiled into the Host, sorted. Operations requiring absent features fail with `feature_unavailable`.

source_contract_digest.description: Digest of the generated source-compatibility inputs (`contracts/sdk/source-contract.json`: Cargo.lock + facade inventory + parity manifest). Negotiated separately from `contract_digest`; both must match for the SDK Client to enter Extended mode.

contract_digest.description: Extension contract digest the Client validates.

extension_protocol_version.description: Extension protocol version the Client was built against.

required_capabilities.description: Extension capabilities the Client requires, sorted by declaration order-free identity; duplicates are a shape violation.

required_features.description: Leaf features the Client requires on the Host, sorted.

EchoAgentClientHello.title: EchoAgentClientHello
EchoAgentClientHello.description: The echo-agent SDK Client hello published under `clientCapabilities._meta.echo_agent`. A Client that sends this object requests Extended mode; the Host enters Extended mode only when every field matches its own [`EchoAgentCapability`]. A missing key means a plain standard ACP Client; a malformed or mismatched hello degrades the connection to Standard mode without failing `initialize` and without creating any extension handles.

AgentSettingsWire.title: AgentSettingsWire
AgentSettingsWire.description: Agent behavior settings projected on the wire. Deliberately minimal: every unsupported knob (memory, human-in-loop, compressor strategy, subagent timeouts, tool toggles) is rejected by `deny_unknown_fields` rather than silently ignored.

oneOf.description: Literal token passed inline. Only for local, single-user machines.
Name of the environment variable holding the token.

CredentialSourceWire.title: CredentialSourceWire
CredentialSourceWire.description: Mutually exclusive credential sourcing (design §10.4). Environment sourcing keeps secrets out of the wire entirely.

LlmApiProtocolWire.title: LlmApiProtocolWire
LlmApiProtocolWire.description: API protocols the core profile can construct. Unlisted protocols fail closed; new protocols extend this enum in a later contract version.

ModelConfigWire.title: ModelConfigWire
ModelConfigWire.description: Wire projection of the model construction settings. Exactly one credential source may be provided — the tagged `credential` field makes inline-token and environment sourcing mutually exclusive by grammar.

base_url.description: Absolute HTTP(S) endpoint of the model API.

temperature.description: Temperature is serialized as a bounded string decimal to avoid float ambiguity across languages.

oneOf.description: Bind the Host default Agent definition. Credential handling stays Host-local, so SDK Clients never transmit secrets for this branch.
Explicit wire projection of the framework construction config.

AgentConfigWire.title: AgentConfigWire
AgentConfigWire.description: Versioned Agent construction config (design §10.4 agent family).

AgentConfigExplicitWire.title: AgentConfigExplicitWire
AgentConfigExplicitWire.description: Explicit Agent construction payload. `config_version` gates evolution: Hosts reject unknown versions with `invalid_config` instead of guessing.

AgentSnapshotWire.title: AgentSnapshotWire
AgentSnapshotWire.description: Typed capability snapshot of one Agent handle.

host_default.description: Whether the definition came from the Host default configuration.

working_dir.description: Absolute working directory bound to new Sessions of this agent, when the definition carries one.

AgentFailureWire.title: AgentFailureWire
AgentFailureWire.description: Lossless wire projection of the framework failure contract (`echo_core::error::AgentFailure`). Categories and terminal kinds are serialized as their framework snake_case names so a later framework variant remains observable instead of collapsing into a generic code.

oneOf.description: The Host process restarted while the run was still active. Interrupted runs never gain a terminal or receipt: `run/get` reports the status, `run/wait` fails with typed `host_exited`, and new work continues from the framework's committed checkpoint only.

failure.description: Lossless framework failure contract (category, terminal kind, retryability, code, bounded message).

RunTerminal.title: RunTerminal
RunTerminal.description: The single authoritative terminal of a settled run. There is no `interrupted` terminal: interruption is a run *status* without terminal or receipt, so a crashed run can never be mistaken for success.

RunReceiptWire.title: RunReceiptWire
RunReceiptWire.description: Typed projection of the framework `TurnReceipt` (design §4.1). Counters use `WireU64` so JavaScript numbers never see an unsafe integer.

elapsed_ms.description: Total wall time of the run in milliseconds.

last_event_sequence.description: Sequence watermark of the last emitted event; aligned with the journal and replay cursors.

RecoveredRunWire.title: RecoveredRunWire
RecoveredRunWire.description: One recovered historical Run with its fresh-generation handles.

last_sequence.description: Last sequence the recovered event history covers.

EventAck.title: EventAck
EventAck.description: Client acknowledgement of consumed live events. The Host counts outstanding notifications per stream against the negotiated `max_outstanding_live_events` window; acknowledgements retire them and resume live delivery after a gap pause. Hosts ignore unknown or un-negotiated ACK notifications without producing a response (ACP notification rules).

last_processed_sequence.description: Highest contiguous sequence the Client has consumed.

AgentCreateRequest.title: AgentCreateRequest
AgentCreateRequest.description: `_echo_agent/agent/create` request. The construction grammar is a versioned typed config, not a free-form value: `host_default` binds the Host's own startup definition; `explicit` carries a strict projection of the framework config. Unsupported builder capabilities (tool callbacks, custom stores, human-in-loop, structured-output contracts) are absent from this versioned surface on purpose — sending unknown fields fails closed as invalid params instead of being silently ignored.

idempotency_id.description: Client-assigned idempotency identity; independent from JSON-RPC ids. The same id plus the same canonical config returns the same handle; the same id with a different config is a typed conflict.

snapshot.description: Immutable construction facts and capability snapshot of the agent.

AgentCloseRequest.title: AgentCloseRequest
AgentCloseRequest.description: `_echo_agent/agent/close` request. In-flight runs settle per the framework's own cancellation semantics; closing never fabricates terminals.

released.description: True when this call released the agent; false when it was already closed (idempotent close).

session_id.description: Stable framework identity to bind the Session to. When omitted the Host assigns one; the response always reports the resolved identity.

working_dir.description: Absolute primary working directory for the new Session.

acp_session_id.description: ACP Session identity of the same Session object, so the SDK Client can address the standard `session/prompt` / `session/cancel` methods on it without a second creation step.

SessionLoadRequest.title: SessionLoadRequest
SessionLoadRequest.description: `_echo_agent/session/load` request: resume a persisted session by framework identity. Only state roots configured for persistence can serve it; loading mints fresh-generation Session/Run/Stream handles and never revives an interrupted Driver.

working_dir.description: Absolute primary working directory for the resumed Session.

acp_session_id.description: ACP Session identity of the resumed Session (see [`SessionCreateResponse::acp_session_id`]).

recovered_sequence.description: Sequence watermark the session recovered to, when replayable.

runs.description: Historical runs recovered for this session, in run start order. Interrupted runs carry `status: "interrupted"` without terminal or receipt; settled runs keep their single authoritative terminal.

oneOf.description: Interactive chat turn with one text message.
Non-interactive execution directive.

RunInput.title: RunInput
RunInput.description: Input of one run: a chat prompt or an execute directive, mirroring the facade's unified turn driver. The payload is typed — the Host never guesses payload tags or applies defaults.

first_event.description: First accepted event of the run, if already available.

stream.description: Live event stream of the run; `_echo_agent/event` notifications and `run/replay` requests address it by this handle.

RunGetResponse.title: RunGetResponse
RunGetResponse.description: Run state snapshot: status, the single authoritative terminal (when settled) and the receipt facts. Never synthesizes a terminal that the framework has not emitted (exactly-one-terminal, design §11.1).

stream.description: Live event stream of the run, when one exists.

RunWaitRequest.title: RunWaitRequest
RunWaitRequest.description: `_echo_agent/run/wait` request: bounded wait for the terminal. A run that is already `interrupted` never settles — the wait responds with the typed `host_exited` error instead of success.

RunCancelRequest.title: RunCancelRequest
RunCancelRequest.description: `_echo_agent/run/cancel` request. Competing with natural completion, the framework's own CAS/terminal semantics decide the unique outcome; the transport never writes a second terminal (design §14.3).

status.description: Status at the time of the call; final state still arrives as events.

RunSteerRequest.title: RunSteerRequest
RunSteerRequest.description: `_echo_agent/run/steer` request: mid-flight steering for chats that support it.

steer_id.description: Steer identity assigned by the framework when accepted.

expected_revision.description: Expected revision for optimistic concurrency; the framework rejects stale writers.

TaskSummary.title: TaskSummary
TaskSummary.description: Projection of one task's identity and state; authoritative state remains in the framework store.

TaskExecuteRequest.title: TaskExecuteRequest
TaskExecuteRequest.description: `_echo_agent/task/execute` request: drive one PlanTask through the framework executor (single authority for scheduling/retry/cancel).

action.description: One of the framework control verbs (`pause`, `resume`, `cancel`).

TaskControlRequest.title: TaskControlRequest
TaskControlRequest.description: `_echo_agent/task/control` request: pause/resume/cancel routed to the framework service.

SubagentDispatchRequest.title: SubagentDispatchRequest
SubagentDispatchRequest.description: `_echo_agent/subagent/dispatch` request. The framework executor remains the only scheduler.

parameters.description: JSON Schema of the tool parameters.

search_modes.description: Search modes the implementation actually supports. Semantic or hybrid searches against an implementation that did not declare them are rejected before any callback is sent.

events.description: Hook events the implementation subscribes to (framework hook event names). Empty means the implementation decides per context.

ExtensionDescriptor.title: ExtensionDescriptor
ExtensionDescriptor.description: Versioned per-kind registration descriptor. Exactly one variant matches the registration's [`ExtensionKind`]; the Host dispatches on this typed snapshot and never guesses trait semantics from free-form JSON (design §12.2). `descriptor_version` gates evolution: unknown versions fail with `invalid_config` instead of being partially applied.

ModelModalityWire.title: ModelModalityWire
ModelModalityWire.description: Model input modality a Tool descriptor may require (wire projection of the framework `ModelInputModality`).

SearchModeWire.title: SearchModeWire
SearchModeWire.description: Search modes a Store descriptor may declare (wire projection of the framework `SearchMode`). Declaring a mode does not downgrade it: the descriptor is a promise the implementation keeps, not a Host-side default.

ExtensionRegisterRequest.title: ExtensionRegisterRequest
ExtensionRegisterRequest.description: `_echo_agent/extension/register` request: register a host-language implementation of a public framework trait (Tool, LlmClient, Store, HumanLoopProvider, Hook, AgentCallback, InterventionCallback, AgentFactory, custom Agent). Registration is owned by the current connection generation: it never survives a Host restart or a reconnect.

descriptor.description: Typed per-kind descriptor snapshot the Host dispatches on.

implementation_id.description: Client-side implementation identity (non-empty). Re-registering the same identity with the same descriptor returns the same handle; a different descriptor is a typed conflict.

timeout.description: Per-registration default deadline for reverse invocations.

released.description: True when this call released the extension; false when it was already released (idempotent unregister).

ExtensionInvocationContext.title: ExtensionInvocationContext
ExtensionInvocationContext.description: Session/run context attached to a reverse invocation, so a language SDK can correlate callbacks with the execution that caused them. Context is diagnostic identity only — it never changes settlement semantics.

ExtensionOperation.title: ExtensionOperation
ExtensionOperation.description: Closed operation set of the extension bridge. Every reverse invocation names exactly one operation; `kind()` binds it to its extension family so the Host can reject an operation dispatched to the wrong kind before any callback leaves the process (design §12.2).

ExtensionInvokeCall.title: ExtensionInvokeCall
ExtensionInvokeCall.description: `_echo_agent/extension/invoke` reverse request (Host -> SDK): invoke a registered implementation. The invocation identity is an independent string — never the JSON-RPC request id — and settles exactly once. The SDK dispatcher runs the host-language code and replies with exactly one of `result`/`stream`/`error`.

deadline.description: Total deadline for this invocation, including stream delivery.

input.description: Typed invocation payload selected by kind + operation (tool input, chat request, store op, ...). The Host never guesses a payload shape from free-form JSON: it constructs this value from real Rust trait arguments.

invocation_id.description: Invocation identity; unique per call, used for cancellation. It is a domain identity independent from any JSON-RPC request id.

operation.description: Which trait operation is being invoked.

stream.description: For streaming operations: the Host-minted stream handle the SDK must acknowledge and address `_echo_agent/extension/stream` notifications to. The SDK never invents stream identities.

oneOf.description: Streaming acknowledgement: the SDK echoes the Host-minted stream handle and delivers the payload through `_echo_agent/extension/stream` notifications.

ExtensionInvokeOutcome.title: ExtensionInvokeOutcome
ExtensionInvokeOutcome.description: One callback outcome. Failures use the typed extension errors; there is no implicit fallback to a built-in implementation (design §12.1).

ExtensionCancelNotice.title: ExtensionCancelNotice
ExtensionCancelNotice.description: `_echo_agent/extension/cancel` reverse notification (Host -> SDK): the framework cancelled an in-flight invocation; the SDK must stop work but still answer the original call with a `cancelled` error or a stream `cancelled` terminal.

ExtensionStreamEvent.title: ExtensionStreamEvent
ExtensionStreamEvent.description: `_echo_agent/extension/stream` event (SDK -> Host notification): one chunk or the single terminal of a streaming callback. Sequence is monotonic per stream and exactly one terminal variant may be emitted by the SDK; the Host enforces exactly-one-terminal and discards late events after settlement with bounded diagnostics only.

FeatureOperationRequest.title: FeatureOperationRequest
FeatureOperationRequest.description: Manifest-identified facade operation using the closed `WireValue` algebra. The operation must match an exact parity-manifest identity and signature.

WorkingDirectory.title: WorkingDirectory
WorkingDirectory.description: Working directory declaration a client may pass for run/session methods that accept one; lossless via `WirePath`.
